title: Eurosystem response to the EU Commission's targeted consultation on the competitiveness of the EU banking sector
summary: The Eurosystem published a comprehensive response to the EU Commission's targeted consultation on EU banking sector competitiveness, advocating for an ambitious reform agenda that preserves resilience while enhancing integration. The document identifies financial fragmentation and lack of scale as key constraints on competitiveness and calls for synchronized progress on banking union components, including finalisation of EDIS with clear implementation timetable, and fostering deeper capital markets via the savings and investment union.
key_points: Eurosystem supports ambitious reform agenda to enhance EU bank competitiveness while preserving financial system resilience
Financial fragmentation and lack of scale are identified as key constraints limiting EU banks' ability to scale up, realize economies of scale, and compete globally
Eurosystem calls for synchronized progress on banking union: EDIS finalization with clear implementation timetable, and fostering capital markets via savings and investment union
HLTF report on prudential framework simplification (endorsed by ECB Governing Council December 2025) forms basis of Eurosystem response
Four-pronged ECB supervisory agenda includes SREP reform, 'next-level supervision' operational initiatives, unified SSM supervisory culture, and supervisory effectiveness assessment

Four guiding principles for simplification: maintain resilience, maintain effectiveness of prudential objectives, foster European harmonization, uphold international cooperation and Basel III implementation
why_it_matters: This document shapes the future regulatory environment for EU banks. Market participants need to understand the direction of EU banking regulation, particularly around integration initiatives (EDIS, capital markets union), prudential framework simplification, and supervisory reforms. The document signals that regulatory changes are coming to address EU banking fragmentation, which will affect competitive dynamics, cross-border operations, and potentially capital requirements for EU banks.
macro_context: The consultation response links bank competitiveness to broader EU economic objectives. Key macro linkages include: stable macroeconomic environment supports consumption and investment financing; large integrated market allows banks to diversify risks; clear rules aligned with international standards preserve confidence and create level playing field. The document references Draghi (2024) and Letta (2024) reports on strengthening Europe's growth and investment.
market_structure_context: Core market structure focus: EU banking market fragmentation, cross-border banking integration barriers, banking union components (EDIS, capital markets union), crisis management framework, regulatory harmonization across member states. Discusses impediments to free flow of capital and liquidity in cross-border groups, and need for fair and timely transfers of resources within groups during stress.
